title: Early trends show women make two-third of revamped rural job scheme workforce
content:
• The revamped rural jobs programme, Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-GRAM G), recorded over 63% women's participation, generating 4.62 crore person-days during its first 20 days (1-20 July).
• Under the VB-GRAM G scheme, the statutory employment guarantee has been expanded to 125 days from 100 days, and the national average daily wage has been raised from ₹298.8 (MGNREGA) to ₹327.4, an average increase of ₹28.6 per day.
• The Centre has allocated ₹95,692.31 crore for the VB-G RAM G scheme in FY27, and under new norms, it will fund 60% of the total cost in most states (90% in North-Eastern and Himalayan states), a shift from MGNREGA's 100% wage cost funding.

title: Budget has buffers to tackle global risks, no need to revisit govt's budget estimates yet, says Sitharaman
content:
• Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that the government does not see a need to revisit its Budget estimates, asserting that adequate fiscal buffers have been created to deal with global uncertainties, including rising oil prices and fertiliser imports.
• Speaking at the NDTV Profit Business Leadership Awards 2026 in Mumbai, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman confirmed that India's economy demonstrates broad-based resilience, with indicators like GST collections, export orders, and digital payments pointing to sustained growth.
• The government has made provisions to absorb the impact of higher fertiliser import prices, ensuring that fertilisers are supplied to farmers at the same price they have paid since COVID.
